content:
Earlier this month, Google launched the all-new Pixel 11 series. Although the phone itself hasn't changed much compared to the previous Pixel 10, it includes several thoughtful user experience improvements. One of them is the addition of new camera processing options, giving you finer control over how your photos turn out.

With the iPhone 18 Pro set to debut soon, I'm hoping Apple will add similar functionality.

The Pixel 11 introduces a new camera feature called "Camera Looks." This feature is somewhat similar to "Photographic Styles" on the iPhone, allowing users to adjust the way the camera takes photos. These adjustments are made before shooting and go beyond just a simple filter.

Google offers many preset style options similar to Apple's, and you can fine-tune the effects for each preset. Additionally, there are several new options that capture emerging photography trends, including Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal.

These Looks are intentionally designed to break away from the over-processed feel of smartphone photos, attempting to recreate the flavour of photos from the old days. As the name suggests, Digi aims to reproduce the low dynamic range, high contrast, and grainy effects characteristic of those small, pocket-sized cameras from the 2010s.

As for Minimal, it takes a completely low-processing approach. Most HDR processing routines won't run, so essentially you'll see what the smartphone image sensor actually captures. You can check out some sample photos at 9to5Google.

In theory, using the ProRAW format on the iPhone, you can revert iPhone photos to a state that seems relatively untouched by post-production, but doing so somewhat goes against the original intent of shooting with a smartphone.

Conclusion

If Apple wants to create the best pocket camera on the market, it needs to understand that not every user wants the same thing. "Photographic Styles" is a good start, but Apple can go further. After all, photography is an art of self-expression, so giving users more options to control the degree of photo processing will be a very important step. Apple should take a page from Google and add a "Minimal" style to the iPhone as well.

What do you think of the iPhone's current photography performance? Do you like Apple's latest "Photographic Styles"? Or do you feel it still falls short? I'd love to hear your thoughts, feel free to share them in the comments section.
